item.title: Nvidia Fallout Looms Over Trump-Xi Meeting
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY) says he wants to know when former CEO Jensen Huang was informed by the US government that the woman he was having an affair with was allegedly involved in Chinese espionage and why Nvidia was not notified sooner. Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, thinks Congress needs to direct its questions to the Commerce Department and, by extension, the National Security Council process staff about what happened with export-control regulations and what may have held them up. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Allen Says US Needs Stronger Export-Control Enforcement
item.description: Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, thinks Congress needs to direct its questions to the Commerce Department and, by extension, the National Security Council process staff about what happened with export-control regulations and what may have held them up. Allen says stronger export controls and beefing up the Department of Commerce are important, including greater enforcement, oversight and investigations. Allen says Trump should make clear to President Xi Jinping that China’s activity involving smuggling and restricted technology could lead Congress to take further action. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief: Lutnick Faces Scrutiny Over Chip Export Controls
item.description: Bloomberg’s Mario Parker joined the show for, The Debrief, to discuss Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick facing scrutiny over what he knew about Nvidia and China, tensions inside the White House and questions about his standing in the administration. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Meeks Says Questions Remain Over Nvidia Warning
item.description: Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY) says he wants to know when former CEO Jensen Huang was informed by the US government that the woman he was having an affair with was allegedly involved in Chinese espionage and why Nvidia was not notified sooner. Rep. Meeks says the issue is not just the affair, but what information might have been given to China and others that could endanger US national security. Rep. Meeks says Congress needs to determine what the administration knew and why Nvidia may not have been notified, as well as examine questions involving Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Ties Attacks on French Fridges to Chinese AI Model
item.description: A Chinese artificial intelligence model was used in recent hacks that disabled refrigerators in French supermarkets, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Salcedo and Yash Roy

item.title: Anwar Faces Malacca Voters After Turbulent Week for Malaysian Politics
item.description: Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim faces his third electoral test this year when the state of Malacca goes to the polls on Saturday, after a frantic week in which a key minister quit over the controversial transfer of jailed former premier Najib Razak to house arrest.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan

item.title: Trump Nominates Bipartisan Slate of CFTC, SEC Commissioners
item.description: President Donald Trump nominated a bipartisan slate of commissioners for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, according to a statement Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Lydia Beyoud and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Nvidia’s Strategy Reset
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was ousted from his post after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Huang, one of the three engineers who founded the chipmaker in 1993, had been under intense pressure since Sunday, when he admitted to a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed International. The Nvidia turmoil rippled through the entire artificial intelligence sector on Thursday, dragging down shares of semiconductor companies.
On today’s episode:
Emily Chang, Host & Executive Producer of Bloomberg’s ‘The Circuit’ Ed Ludlow, Bloomberg Tech Co-Host Lauren Cassidy, Founder & Chief Investment Officer, Founders 100 ETF Nina Trentmann, Bloomberg News Senior Editor & CFO Briefing Editor (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SEC Investigates T1 Energy’s Disclosures of Tax Credits
item.description: T1 Energy Inc. said it’s being probed by the US Securities and Exchange Commission over the solar company’s disclosures related to its eligibility for clean energy manufacturing tax credits and other accounting matters.
item.dc:creator: Mark Chediak

item.title: Burnham Says Cameron Wrong to Dismiss Brexit’s Hit to UK Economy
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said former premier David Cameron was wrong to argue that Britain’s economic problems are “nothing to do with Brexit.”
item.dc:creator: Lucy White and Alex Wickham

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Ousted by Board
item.description: Jensen Huang, the preeminent face of the AI infrastructure boom, was ousted from his post after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Bloomberg’s team of AI, Tech, and Geoeconomics experts break down the market moving announcement. Host of ‘The Curcuit’, Emily Chang, recounts her conversation with Huang from just one month ago where he spoke about the “high standard” of responsibility for a CEO. Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow explains how Huang’s ousting will impact the company and the potential forthcoming investigations. Plus, Bloomberg Economics Geoeconomics Technology Analyst Michael Deng breaks down how this might impact both sides of the US-China AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Joins Groundswell of Support for AI Chip Control Measures
item.description: OpenAI is backing a bipartisan effort in Congress to block China’s access to artificial intelligence chips and curb China’s access to chipmaking equipment, adding support to legislation gaining momentum after the scandal that toppled Jensen Huang as Nvidia Corp.’s chief executive officer.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland, Alicia Diaz and Emily Birnbaum

item.title: Elon Musk Powers Ahead Despite a Costly Midterms Rout
item.description: If the threat of Democratic oversight is prompting his empire to shift course, it isn’t showing yet.
item.dc:creator: Ted Mann

item.title: Trump Bets Shaky Iran Status Quo Will Hold After Midterm Loss
item.description: President Donald Trump has floated a new strategy for his war against Iran: leave the conflict in limbo and walk away.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin, Courtney McBride and Fiona MacDonald

item.title: Hegseth Awards Soldier Who Admonished His Party on Veterans Day
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has commended the soldier who loudly called for the Pentagon chief and his party to maintain decorum near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Trump Suggests Xi Unlikely to Release Hong Kong’s Jimmy Lai
item.description: President Donald Trump indicated he is not optimistic about the prospects of getting Chinese President Xi Jinping to agree to release imprisoned Hong Kong businessman and activist Jimmy Lai.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Joe Rogan Blames GOP’s Texas Wipeout on ‘Crazy Laws’ on THC
item.description: Joe Rogan is offering a new explanation for the stunning electoral losses suffered last week by Texas Republicans: the state’s strict cannabis laws.
item.dc:creator: Joe Lovinger

item.title: Senate Democrat Defends Oversight After US Attorney Threat
item.description: A key Senate Democrat is defending his authority to probe White House dealings and accused the administration of intimidation after one of President Donald Trump’s US attorneys threatened him with a Justice Department investigation.
item.dc:creator: Celine Castronuovo

item.title: Dutch Lawmakers Pass Wealth Bill That Risks Toppling Coalition
item.description: The lower house of the Dutch parliament passed a left-leaning bill that would increase the tax burden on the wealthy, and risks toppling Prime Minister Rob Jetten’s coalition.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Van Oosterom and Charlotte Hughes-Morgan

item.title: Iran Plot Against UK-Based Reporter Marks Shift in Sabotage Threat
item.description: Two Iranian nationals were found guilty of engaging in conduct likely to assist Iran’s intelligence agency, in the latest case involving foreign spy services ordering surveillance and sabotage in Britain.
item.dc:creator: Upmanyu Trivedi
